decisions.reason: It is close to the firm’s core equipment and lab-processing knowledge, has remained visibly marketed across two years, and the firm’s strong in-house R&D makes it likely management expects further learning and improvement rather than withdrawal.

An orthopedic shoe last is distant from the firm’s established dental and hearing-system knowledge base, so despite having R&D the firm is less able to absorb market feedback and is more likely to reallocate resources to closer, more learnable product lines.

A post-curing unit fits well with the firm’s digital manufacturing and device-processing capabilities, and its internal R&D and broad medical-technology portfolio support continued refinement even if it was only lightly featured on the website in its launch year.
